description: A scripting and sequencing platform: ten short scripts, eight of them fired by the trigger inputs, driving four triggers and four control voltages

params.text: A value the scripts can read with the PARAM operator, 0 to 16383 across the knob's travel, standing for 0V to 10V
Short-press to open the scene view, where the scenes stored in this module can be loaded
Click to reclaim a grid that has been taken by another module; the right-click menu is where a grid is first chosen

inputs.text: A rising edge above 2.21V here runs the script of the same number; the response happens on the sample the trigger arrives, not at the module's downsampled rate
A value the scripts can read with the IN operator, 0 to 16383 across 0V to 10V

outputs.text: One of four trigger outputs, 0V low and 10V high, driven by the TR operators in a script
One of four control outputs, 0V to 10V, driven by the CV operators in a script

notes: click the screen to give it the keyboard; a ring is drawn round it while it has focus, and every keystroke then goes to this module instead of to Rack until you click away.
the Tab key cycles between three modes: one where commands run as you type them, one where scripts are written, and one where pattern data is edited. The right-click menu has an item for each.
a faderbank module placed immediately beside this one becomes a parameter expander, its sixteen faders readable with the FADER operator. Up to four of them can be chained on either side.
a grid can be connected from the right-click menu, but unlike the other modules here this one works from a computer keyboard alone.
a scene is a whole set of scripts and patterns. Up to 32 of them are stored inside this module and saved with the patch; the right-click menu also imports and exports them as text files.
menu: Theme: Red, Orange, Yellow, White — sets the colour of the screen text and the panel lamps
Keyboard layout — chooses how Rack's keystrokes are turned into the USB scancodes the firmware reads, for keyboards that are not US English
Import scenes — reads scenes from a text file of the kind the hardware module uses
Export scenes — writes the stored scenes out as a text file of the kind the hardware module uses
LIVE mode — switches the screen to the mode where typed commands run at once; F12 with the screen focused does it too
EDIT mode — switches the screen to the mode where scripts are written; Alt and F1 with the screen focused does it too
TRACKER mode — switches the screen to the mode where pattern data is edited; F11 with the screen focused does it too
Cycle LIVE/EDIT/TRACKER — steps to the next of the three screen modes; the Tab key with the screen focused does it too
SCENE READ mode — opens the scene loading view; Escape with the screen focused does it too
SCENE WRITE mode — opens the scene saving view; Alt and Escape with the screen focused does it too
Previous script/page/value/scene — steps back; the left bracket key with the screen focused does it too
Next script/page/value/scene — steps forward; the right bracket key with the screen focused does it too
HELP mode — opens the on-screen reference for the operators; Alt and H with the screen focused does it too
Firmware Tools — opens a submenu naming the firmware and its version, with the input and output rate settings, a screenshot command, and the firmware reload commands
Input rate — sets how often the module reads its jacks, from 1x at the audio sample rate down to /16; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Output rate — sets how often the module writes its jacks, from 1x at the audio sample rate down to /16; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Save PNG screenshot — writes a picture of the module to disk; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Switch Firmware — loads a different firmware build into the module; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Hot Reload — reloads the firmware and keeps both the working memory and the stored presets; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Reload & Restart — reloads the firmware, discards the working memory and keeps the stored presets; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Clear NVRAM — wipes the module's stored presets and keeps the working memory; found on the Firmware Tools submenu
Device Connection — lists the hardware and virtual grids the module can attach to; pick one to connect it, and the USB jack on the panel then shows a plug in it
